user.title: BACnet IP Network Configuration
user.description: Configure the local BACnet/IP network interface. To add a specific device by IP address, fill in the target address below. Leave it empty to discover all devices on the network automatically.

data_description.local_ip: Leave empty to use the network interface Home Assistant itself uses (recommended). Only fill in the IP address of this Home Assistant server to use another interface, optionally with its subnet prefix (e.g. 192.168.1.100/24). This is NOT the BACnet device address.
data_description.target_address: IP address of the BACnet device to add (e.g. 192.168.1.50 or 192.168.1.50:47808). Leave empty to discover devices automatically via Who-Is broadcast.
data_description.target_device_id: BACnet Device Object Instance number (DOI). Only used when a target address is specified. Leave at 0 to auto-detect.
data_description.use_bbmd: Enable this if BACnet devices are on another subnet/VLAN and a BBMD is available.
data_description.bbmd_address: IP address and port of the BBMD (e.g. 192.168.2.1:47808).
data_description.bbmd_ttl: Time-to-live for the Foreign Device Registration in seconds.

discovery.title: Device Discovery
discovery.description: Searching for BACnet devices on the network. This may take a few seconds...

data_description.device_id: Choose the device you want to add to Home Assistant.

select_objects.title: Select BACnet Objects
select_objects.description: Tick object types to import all their objects, pick single objects in the list, or tick Select all objects to import everything.

data.select_types: Import all objects of these types

data_description.device_name: Name for this device in Home Assistant. Pre-filled with the BACnet objectName.
data_description.select_types: Every object of a ticked type is imported, together with the objects you pick below.
data_description.selected_objects: Type to search by object type (for example AI or BO), instance or name, and pick the objects you want in Home Assistant. Nothing is selected yet.
data_description.share_usage: Ticked by default; untick to send nothing. Once a day, sends this device's manufacturer, model and firmware, whether COV and ReadPropertyMultiple work, the number of objects per type and how it is connected (direct or BBMD), plus the integration and Home Assistant version and a random installation ID. Never addresses, names or values. Used to grow the tested devices list. [Privacy policy]({privacy_url})

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure BACnet connection
reconfigure.description: Change the network settings or the address of this BACnet device. Entities, their history and all options are kept; the integration reloads with the new settings.

data_description.local_ip: Leave empty to use the network interface Home Assistant itself uses (recommended). Only fill in the IP address of this Home Assistant server to use another interface, optionally with its subnet prefix (e.g. 192.168.1.100/24). This is NOT the BACnet device address.
data_description.use_bbmd: Enable this if BACnet devices are on another subnet/VLAN and a BBMD is available.
data_description.bbmd_address: IP address and port of the BBMD (e.g. 192.168.2.1:47808).
data_description.bbmd_ttl: Time-to-live for the Foreign Device Registration in seconds.
data_description.device_address: IP address (and optional port) of the BACnet device, e.g. 192.168.1.50 or 192.168.1.50:47808, or a routed address such as 20000:1.

init.title: BACnet Integration Options
init.description: Configure update behaviour, entity naming and per-object settings for this device.

data.use_description: Use description (property id 28) instead of name
data.rescan_objects: Rescan device and manage BACnet object selection

data_description.enable_cov: When enabled, the integration subscribes to COV notifications. If the device does not support COV or subscription fails, polling is used as fallback.
data_description.cov_increment: Minimum value change on the device before a COV notification is sent (applies to analog objects only). Set to 0 to use the device's default. Example: 0.5 means a notification is sent when the value changes by at least 0.5.
data_description.polling_interval: How often all objects are polled, in seconds (minimum 10). Polling always runs; COV only adds faster updates in between.
data_description.use_description: When checked, entities will be named using the BACnet 'description' property (ID 28) instead of 'objectName' (ID 77).
data_description.rescan_objects: Rereads the device's current Object_List so you can add objects that weren't selected during setup, or pick up objects added to the device since. Currently imported objects stay selected by default.
data_description.live_metadata_properties: Properties that get their own live COV-Property subscription instead of the periodic re-read. Each one is an extra subscription on the device, and not every device supports it.
data_description.share_usage: Ticked by default; untick to send nothing. Once a day, sends this device's manufacturer, model and firmware, whether COV and ReadPropertyMultiple work, the number of objects per type and how it is connected (direct or BBMD), plus the integration and Home Assistant version and a random installation ID. Never addresses, names or values. Used to grow the tested devices list. [Privacy policy]({privacy_url})

rescan_objects.title: Manage BACnet Objects
rescan_objects.description: Add or remove objects. Everything you leave empty stays as it is: submitting without changes keeps the current selection. Objects the device no longer has are dropped. Settings of removed objects are remembered.

data.select_types: Add all objects of these types

data_description.add_objects: Objects not imported yet; those marked NEW. Type to search by abbreviation (AI, BO 3), instance or name.
data_description.select_types: Every object of a ticked type that is not imported yet is added. The number is how many that are.
data_description.remove_objects: Imported objects to remove. Type to search.

domain_mapping.title: Customize objects
domain_mapping.description: Pick the BACnet objects whose entity type, COV setting or climate temperature sensor you want to change. Type to search. Objects that already have a custom setting are already picked; objects not picked use the defaults.

customize_objects.title: Customize objects
customize_objects.description: Per object: the Home Assistant entity type, whether COV is used, and — for objects that are already a climate entity — which object provides the room temperature. Changed an object to climate just now? Save, then open the options again to pick its temperature sensor. Extra properties: pick properties (for example Minimum On Time or High Limit) to show as their own entity; type any other property by name or number under other properties.

error.invalid_polling_interval: The polling interval must be at least 10 seconds.
error.no_objects_found: No readable BACnet objects were found on this device.
error.unknown_property: Unknown BACnet property. Use names such as minimumOnTime or minimum-on-time, or numbers such as 67, separated by commas.
error.no_objects_selected: Select at least one object, or keep some of the imported ones.

abort.cannot_connect: Could not reach the BACnet device to rescan its object list. Make sure the device is online and try again.

menu_options.remove: Remove the overrides (use the default types)

device_unreachable.title: {device} is not responding
device_unreachable.description:
Home Assistant has not received data from the BACnet device {device} for several polls, and reconnecting did not help. Its entities are unavailable until it answers again.

Check that the device is powered and on the network, that its address is still correct (you can change it via Reconfigure), and — when a BBMD is used — that the BBMD is reachable. This message disappears by itself once the device responds.

share_usage.title: Help grow the tested devices list

confirm.title: Share usage statistics?
confirm.description:
This integration can send a small report once a day about your BACnet devices: manufacturer, model and firmware, whether COV and ReadPropertyMultiple work, and the number of objects per type. Never addresses, names or values. It helps decide which devices get tested and supported.

Tick to share for all your BACnet devices, untick to keep it off. You are only asked once and can change it per device in its options. [Privacy policy]({privacy_url})

write_failed.message: The BACnet device rejected the write to {object}. Check the Home Assistant log for the reason (for example a wrong write priority or an object that is not writable).

not_a_bacnet_object.message: {entity_id} is not a BACnet object entity of this integration.

not_a_schedule.message: {entity_id} is not a BACnet Schedule object.

unknown_property.message: Unknown BACnet property: {property}. Use the property name (e.g. minimumOnTime) or its number (e.g. 67).

invalid_object.message: Give both an object type (name or number) and an instance when a device is given.

no_bacnet_device.message: Pick a BACnet device of this integration in the Device field.

not_a_trend_log.message: {entity_id} is not a BACnet Trend Log entity.

relinquish.name: Relinquish
relinquish.description: Release Home Assistant's command on a BACnet object (writes Null at a priority level), so lower priorities or the Relinquish Default take over.

priority.name: Priority
priority.description: Priority level to release (1-16). Defaults to the device's Write Priority.

write_value.name: Write value
write_value.description: Write a value once: an object's present value at a chosen priority (without changing the device's Write Priority setting), or any other property.

value.name: Value
value.description: Value to write. Binary objects: 0 = inactive, 1 = active. Other properties take a number, true/false or text.

priority.name: Priority
priority.description: Priority level to write at (1-16). Defaults to the device's Write Priority.

property.name: Property
property.description: BACnet property to write, by name (minimumOnTime) or number (67). Without it: the property an extra-property entity shows, otherwise the present value; the priority only applies to the present value.

object_type.name: Object type
object_type.description: Only with Device: type of the object to use, by name (analog-value, trend-log) or number. Reaches objects that were not imported.

instance.name: Object instance
instance.description: Only with Device: instance number of the object.

device.name: Device
device.description: Only for objects that aren't imported: the BACnet device. Then also give the object type and instance; the target entity is ignored.

read_schedule.name: Read schedule
read_schedule.description: Read a BACnet Schedule object: weekly schedule, exception schedule (with the dates of referenced calendars), default value, effective period and the objects it controls. Returns the data as a response.

write_schedule.name: Write schedule
write_schedule.description: Change parts of a BACnet Schedule object, using the same data shape read_schedule returns. Fields left out are not touched. The schedule is read back afterwards; the action fails if the device rejected the change or stored something different.

weekly_schedule.name: Weekly schedule
weekly_schedule.description: Weekdays (monday … sunday) mapped to a list of entries, each with a time and a value. Only the days given are changed; a value of null releases the schedule to its default. If the device refuses single-day writes, pass all seven days.

exception_schedule.name: Exception schedule
exception_schedule.description: Complete list of exceptions, replacing the existing one. Each has a period (date, date_range, week_n_day or calendar_reference), a priority (1-16) and time_values. If this would remove exceptions the device currently has, the action fails and lists them, unless Allow removal is on.

schedule_default.name: Default value
schedule_default.description: Value used when no weekly or exception entry applies.

effective_period.name: Effective period
effective_period.description: Start and end date between which the schedule is active. A date is YYYY-MM-DD, or an object with year, month, day and weekday where null means any.

allow_removal.name: Allow removal
allow_removal.description: Allow the exception schedule to be written even if that removes exceptions the device currently has.

read_property.name: Read property
read_property.description: Read any property of a BACnet object and return it as response data.

property.name: Property
property.description: BACnet property to read, by name (minimumOnTime, eventState) or number (67). Without it: the property an extra-property entity shows, otherwise the present value.

array_index.name: Array index
array_index.description: Read one element of an array property (0 = number of elements).

object_type.name: Object type
object_type.description: Only with Device: type of the object to use, by name (analog-value, trend-log) or number. Reaches objects that were not imported.

instance.name: Object instance
instance.description: Only with Device: instance number of the object.

device.name: Device
device.description: Only for objects that aren't imported: the BACnet device. Then also give the object type and instance; the target entity is ignored.

read_trend_log.name: Read trend log
read_trend_log.description: Read the records of a BACnet Trend Log and return them as response data. Target a Trend Log entity, or pick the device and give the instance for a Trend Log that isn't imported. Only records with a time and a value are returned.

device.name: Device
device.description: Only for a Trend Log that isn't imported: the BACnet device.

instance.name: Trend Log instance
instance.description: Only with Device: instance number of the Trend Log object.

start.name: Start
start.description: Return records from this time on (device local time). Without it, the most recent records are returned.
